To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the total level of fatty acids in adipose tissue is not correlated with the cardiovascular disease risk factors, and that the concentrations of individual fatty acids are only weakly correlated with these factors.
the total amount of fatty acid isomeric content in adipose tissue was not related to the risk factors for cardiovascular diseases.
the concentrations of trans and cis isomers in adipocytes are not related to the risk of cardiovascular disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationships between the concentrations of isomeric (cis and trans) fatty acids in adipose tissue and cardiovascular risk factors.
the relationship between the fatty acid composition of human adipose tissue and clinical risk factors for coronary artery disease.
the relationship of isomeric trans fatty acids to the risk of cardiovascular disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence that the fatty acid isomers present in adipose tissue are related to any of the cardiovascular risk factors measured.
the adipose tissue levels of fatty acid isomer groups or individual isomers do not correlate with cardiovascular risk factors.
the concentrations of fatty acid isomeric forms in human adipose tissues are not correlated with any of the risk factors for cardiovascular diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the total level of fatty acids in human tissue or a factor that is representative of fatty acids of dietary origin is not significantly associated with cardiovascular risk factors.
the total percentage of fatty acid isomer in adipose tissue was not significantly related to cardiovascular disease risk factors, but that some individual isomers were correlated with these factors.

the fatty acid isomers present in adipose tissue of free-living adults were generally representative of those in the diet and that there is no evidence to support the hypothesis that isomers of either dietary or endogenous origin have a major influence on the development of cardiovascular disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in contrast with the situation in animal models, the levels of trans and cis fatty acid isomers of dietary origins in human adipose tissues are not associated with the risk of coronary heart disease.
the total level of isomeric fats in adipose tissue does not reflect the total dietary intake of trans fatty acids, which is a major concern.
the concentrations of fatty acid isomeric forms in adipose tissue are not significantly correlated with any of the cardiovascular disease risk factors.
